subtopics.title: Convert First — the Step That Decides the Mark

questions.question: One square metre is equal to:
A cubic metre of water is:
1 750 mm expressed in metres is:
Which pair of habits does the lesson name as protecting measurement marks?
options: Round each step to one decimal as you go
Write the unit on every line, and round only once at the end
Estimate first, then adjust the answer to look sensible

subtopics.title: Fencing the Garden — Perimeter as a Shopping List

questions.question: The perimeter of a garden 14 m by 9 m is:
44 m of mesh is needed and rolls hold 25 m. How many rolls must be bought, and why?
options: 2 rolls, because materials must always be rounded up to cover the job
1 roll, because 1,76 rounds to 2 only above 1,8
1,76 rolls, because that is the exact answer

questions.question: Poles stand every 2 m around the closed 46 m boundary. The number of poles is:
options: 24, because you always add one pole
23, because a closed boundary needs as many poles as gaps
22, because the gate replaces a pole

questions.question: The total cost of 2 rolls at R749,00 and 23 poles at R72,00 is:

subtopics.title: Tiles and Paint — Area, Coverage and Waste

questions.question: The floor of a room 4,0 m by 3,6 m has an area of:
With a 10% waste allowance added, 14,4 m² of floor needs how many 1,8 m² boxes of tiles?
The wall area of the room is found by:
options: Length × breadth, the same as the floor
Perimeter of the room × wall height

questions.question: After subtracting the door (1,89 m²) and window (1,68 m²) from 39,52 m², two coats at 8 m² per litre require:

subtopics.title: The Water Tank — Volume, Litres and How Long It Lasts

questions.question: A cylindrical tank is 1,2 m across. The radius used in the formula is:
Using π = 3,142, the volume of the tank (radius 0,6 m, height 1,8 m) is about:
A household of four using 340 ℓ a day empties the 2 036 ℓ tank in:
options: 5 complete days, because the sixth day runs dry before it ends

questions.question: A 75 m² roof catching 8 mm of rain collects:

subtopics.title: Walking Around It, Covering It, Filling It

questions.question: "How far around?" is a question about:
Answering 23 m for the perimeter of the 14 m by 9 m garden means the learner:
options: Used the area formula by mistake
Added the two sides but forgot to double, buying half the fence needed

questions.question: The little raised 3 on a volume answer tells you that:
options: You are counting cubes, because three dimensions were multiplied
The answer must be divided by three

subtopics.title: Buying Enough Paint Without Buying Too Much

questions.question: Buying 2 rolls of 25 m mesh for a 44 m job leaves:
options: 6 m unused, which a good answer mentions as waste

questions.question: Which measurement must NOT be used to work out how much paint the walls need?
The rule stated for buying materials is:
options: Round to the nearest whole number
Round down and top up later if needed

questions.question: Why is 10% added to the floor area before dividing by the box coverage?
options: Because tiles are cut at the edges and some crack
Because VAT must be added to the area
Because the boxes are sometimes underfilled
Because the room might be measured wrongly

subtopics.title: How Many Days Does the Tank Give You

questions.question: Forgetting to halve the diameter before squaring makes the volume answer:
The tank holding 2,036 m³ holds, in litres:
Which statement correctly contrasts the two rounding decisions in this lesson?
options: Both round up, to be on the safe side
Both round down, because shops sell whole units
Rounding depends only on whether the decimal is above 0,5
Materials round UP because you must have enough; days and whole items round DOWN because you cannot have part of one

questions.question: What should the final line of a measurement answer look like?
options: Just the number, since the working shows the rest
A sentence a real family could act on — how many days, tins or rands
